It also favors compositions where the main lines or horizon are noticeably tilted (diagonal structure) rather than level or absent. It is weak on small or distant subjects and on scenes with no single main subject. The tilt and subject-size preferences are at the 95th percentile or above for this unit but not for its similar units, so they appear particular to it.

real_s1.explanation: The unit prefers photos with a single, clearly defined main subject that is large in the frame (more than a quarter of the photo), sharp, and well lit. It is weak on small, distant subjects and on scenes without one main subject. It is also notably more active when the main straight lines or horizon are tilted, giving a diagonal composition, than when they are level or absent. The tilt preference and the subject-size preference are where this unit stands out from its similar units, which sit well below the 95th percentile on those rows.

null_s1.explanation: This unit responds to photos with a single, clear, well-defined main subject, such as an animal, insect or vehicle, rather than scenes with no single subject. It responds more when the subject is sharp and of moderate size. It also leans toward subjects shown in side profile (facing left or right) rather than facing toward or away from the camera, and toward tilted lines or warm tints. The 'no single main subject' contrasts are the most distinctive, because the similar units are low on them.

null_s2.explanation: The unit responds most to photos with a single clear, sharp, well-defined main subject, typically a side-on animal or object such as an insect, amphibian, snake or vehicle. It responds weakly to photos with no single main subject, like scattered scenes or textures. It also leans a little toward subjects in profile (facing left or right rather than toward the camera), tilted lines and warm tints, but these effects are weaker. The 'no single main subject' contrasts are large and mostly not shared by the similar units. However, each rests on only 5 to 7 photos, so they may not repeat as reliably on new photos.
